title: Resolving support-mismatch by local basis rotation in variational Monte Carlo
authors: Jia-Lin Chen, Zhen Fan, Canhui Yan, Yantao Wu, Tao Xiang
abstract: Real-time dynamics after a local quench by a charged operator encodes the response functions measured in spectroscopic experiments, yet they have long posed a challenge for variational Monte Carlo calculations. The obstacle is a support mismatch: the projective action by a charged local operator forces an exponentially large number of configurations to vanish, but these configurations may still contribute to the dynamics, biasing the estimators and freezing the evolution at the very first step. This difficulty is an artifact of the chosen sampling basis, and the support mismatch generated by a charged local operator is itself local. We demonstrate that the missing support can be restored by a local rotation of the sampling basis, without changing the underlying variational dynamics. We propose a local basis-rotation sampling scheme that resolves the support-mismatch problem and can be readily incorporated into existing variational Monte Carlo algorithms. Benchmarks show that rotation sampling accurately captures long-time quantum dynamics, enabling variational Monte Carlo calculations of dynamical structure factors in one dimension and unbiased local-operator quench dynamics in two dimensions. We also show that this resolution of the support-mismatch problem extends beyond real-time dynamics, and may also be helpful for ground state variational Monte Carlo calculations.
summary: The paper introduces a technique called local basis rotation sampling to overcome the 'support mismatch' problem encountered in Variational Monte Carlo simulations. This bias arises when local quenches force certain quantum configurations to have zero amplitude, causing numerical instability. By rotating the sampling basis locally, the authors restore these missing contributions, allowing for accurate simulation of long-time dynamics and spectral properties in various spin models.
main_problem: The primary challenge is resolving 'support mismatch' bias in Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) simulations when calculating real-time dynamics after a local quench by a charged operator.
main_result: A novel local basis rotation sampling scheme successfully resolves this support-mismatch problem, enabling accurate variational calculations of long-time quantum dynamics and dynamical structure factors.
method: The authors propose augmenting the variational state with a helper state and applying a one-site unitary rotation to the sampling basis. This restores contributions from zero-amplitude configurations without altering the underlying physics.
model_or_system: The method is tested on various models, including the XY model (1D and 2D) and the Heisenberg chain, simulating local-operator quenches in these quantum spin systems.
key_observables: Dynamical structure factors (DSF), quench-site magnetization $\langle S_{z}^i(t) angle$, and energy drift ($\Delta E/|E|$).
important_parameters: The dynamics are studied over long time scales ($t_{	ext{max}}=40$) and in various dimensions (1D, 2D).
main_assumptions: The support mismatch is an artifact of the chosen sampling basis, which can be corrected by a local rotation.
figures_summary: Figures compare standard tVMC/p-tVMC simulations that freeze at $t=0$ due to bias against those using rotation sampling (rot-tVMC/rot-p-tVMC), showing the latter accurately tracking exact or reference results for magnetization and spectra.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the support mismatch problem in tVMC, then introduces the local basis rotation as a solution. It validates this approach by benchmarking against known solvable models (XY chain) and comparing spectral functions with established methods (ABACUS). The technique is shown to be applicable both for real-time dynamics and ground-state optimization.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial, general numerical tool for simulating non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in strongly correlated systems where standard VMC estimators fail due to nodal structure or local quenching operators.
